```{r load_package, include=FALSE}
devtools::load_all()
```

Read and assimilate Best & GIlbert diet data for Pacific Halibut

```{r}

# 1. Convert PDF pages to high-resolution PNG images (300+ DPI recommended)
# This creates a PNG file for each page in your working directory
pdf_images <- pdftools::pdf_convert(here::here("data","Pages_Best_Gilbert_Pacific_halibut.pdf"), dpi = 300)

# 2. Run OCR across all the generated page images
ocr_text <- tesseract::ocr(pdf_images)

# 3. Put raw text into a tibble split by lines
ocr_tibble <- tidyr::tibble(page = seq_along(ocr_text), text = ocr_text) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(text, sep = "\n") %>%
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(text, "\\S")) # Remove empty rows

nrow.tibble <- nrow(ocr_tibble)

num_numeric_cols <- 12
# 4. Further parse columns using string separation (adjust regex to match your table)
final_table <- ocr_tibble[5:nrow.tibble,] %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      # Extract everything before the first sequence of numbers
      species = stringr::str_extract(text, "^[^0-9]+") %>% stringr::str_trim(),
      # Remove the species name and split remaining numbers
      numbers = stringr::str_remove(text, "^[^0-9]+") %>% stringr::str_trim()
    ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(text!="Unidentified") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(numbers=gsub("[|]", "1", numbers)) %>%
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(
      numbers,
      delim = " ",
      names = paste0("value_", 1:num_numeric_cols),
      cols_remove = TRUE,
      too_few = "align_end"
    )

readr::write_csv(final_table, here::here("outputs","Best_Gilbert_Pacific_halibut.csv"))

```
